facts.text: The hotel opened in 1926.
facts.excerpt: Since opening its doors in 1926, InterContinental New York Barclay has been intertwined with the city’s vibrant history

facts.text: The hotel was originally part of Grand Central Terminal's urban design plan.
facts.excerpt: Originally part of Grand Central Terminal’s urban design plan

facts.text: The Barclay was designed in neo-Federal, American Colonial style by Cross and Cross, the firm behind the Tiffany & Co. building.
facts.excerpt: designed in neo-Federal, American Colonial style by Cross and Cross—the firm behind the iconic Tiffany & Co. building

facts.text: The hotel has a grand staircase, Federalist-inspired details and an intricate lobby ceiling.
facts.excerpt: honoring its 1926 heritage with a grand staircase, Federalist-inspired details, and an intricate lobby ceiling

facts.text: Ernest Hemingway completed the final revisions of For Whom The Bell Tolls at the hotel.
facts.excerpt: It was here that he completed the final revisions of For Whom The Bell Tolls.

facts.text: In 1945 The Barclay introduced the first-ever hotel lobby birdcage, filled with songbirds.
facts.excerpt: In January 1945, The Barclay introduced the first-ever hotel lobby birdcage, filled with canaries, finches, and other songbirds

facts.text: Bill Clinton used The Barclay as his New York campaign headquarters in 1996.
facts.excerpt: In 1996, Bill Clinton used The Barclay as his New York campaign headquarters during his re-election bid

facts.text: The hotel is near Grand Central Station.
